note: Verified field events with conceptual or methodological date in 1850-1930, from two blind harvests (Wikipedia; MacTutor biographies and SEP) plus the seed events in the same period, matched into clusters. Verification: one Opus pass per item (real / real_out_of_scope / not_event). Not checked by a human. The Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Britannica could not be read.

events.name: Graph theory birth
events.summary: Kirchhoff's circuit trees, Cayley's tree counting, and the four colour problem made graphs a subject, with Koenig's 1936 book as first textbook.
keyWorks: Kirchhoff, Ueber die Aufloesung der Gleichungen, 1847
Cayley, On the theory of the analytical forms called trees, 1857
Kuratowski, Sur le probleme des courbes gauches en topologie, 1930

evidence.paraphrase: Kuratowski in 1930 showed the three-cottage problem has no solution.

W87.notes: Kirchhoff, Ann. Phys. 1847, doi 10.1002/andp.18471481202. Cayley, Phil. Mag. 1857 (in Collected Papers). Kuratowski, Fund. Math. 15 (1930), doi 10.4064/fm-15-1-271-283. Euler 1736 is a precursor; the field forms in 1852-78, when Sylvester named the 'graph'. A diffuse event.

events.name: Riemannian geometry
events.summary: Riemann generalised Gauss's intrinsic surface geometry to n-dimensional manifolds with a metric, making curvature an intrinsic notion.
keyWorks: Riemann, Ueber die Hypothesen, welche der Geometrie zu Grunde liegen, 1854 (publ. 1868)

evidence.paraphrase: Riemann in 1854 studied the intrinsic geometry of smooth surfaces and found another non-Euclidean geometry.
The 1854 lecture defined what is now called a Riemannian space and curvature tensor, unpublished until 1868.

W1.notes: Genuine birth by abstraction. Lecture given 1854, published 1868 in Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen (no DOI). The 1861 date is the Paris prize essay, which is fine as a methodological date. DUPLICATE of M2: merge them.

M2.notes: DUPLICATE of W1: merge them. 1868 is the publication date, not an institutional date.

events.name: General relativity and tensor geometry
events.summary: Riemannian geometry and the tensor calculus are adopted as the language of gravitation, then fed back as a source of problems for geometry and analysis.

events.name: Tensor calculus (Ricci)
events.summary: Christoffel and Ricci developed coordinate-independent calculus of tensors, systematised by Ricci and Levi-Civita.
keyWorks: Christoffel, Ueber die Transformation der homogenen Differentialausdruecke, Crelle 1869
Ricci and Levi-Civita, Methodes de calcul differentiel absolu, Math. Ann. 1900

evidence.paraphrase: Ricci developed absolute differential calculus between 1887 and 1896 and popularised it with Levi-Civita in 1900.
Ricci developed the calculus in 1884-1894.

W71.notes: Christoffel Crelle 70 (1869) and Ricci-Levi-Civita Math. Ann. 54 (1900) confirmed. Duplicate of M59.

M59.notes: Duplicate of W71; Math. Ann. 54 (1900) confirmed.

events.name: Ideals and algebraic number theory
events.summary: Dedekind replaced Kummer's ideal numbers by sets of algebraic integers closed under addition and multiplication, restoring unique factorization.
keyWorks: Dedekind, supplement X to Dirichlet's Vorlesungen ueber Zahlentheorie, 2nd ed. 1871; 3rd ed. 1879

evidence.paraphrase: Ideal theory first appeared in supplements to Dirichlet's lectures, dated 1879 on the page.

M9.notes: Dedekind's ideals as sets are a genuine abstraction and are in scope. Supplement X of Dirichlet's Vorlesungen (1871) is a standard citation. Hilbert's Zahlbericht (1897) is a better institutional date. Overlaps W15.

events.name: Riemann surfaces
events.summary: Riemann treated multi-valued algebraic functions as single-valued functions on a covering surface, bringing topology into complex analysis.
keyWorks: Riemann, Grundlagen fuer eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen, 1851
Riemann, Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, 1857
Weyl, Die Idee der Riemannschen Flaeche, 1913

evidence.paraphrase: Riemann surfaces arose in the 1850s from the study of Abelian integrals.
Riemann's 1851 thesis introduced topological methods into complex function theory.

W22.notes: Riemann 1851 dissertation and Crelle 54 (1857) confirmed; brings topology (connectivity, genus) into complex function theory. Evidence URL (Abstract_algebra page) is the wrong source.

M1.notes: Crelle 54 (1857), doi 10.1515/crll.1857.54.115. The 1851 thesis has no DOI. A genuine fusion of function theory and topology.

events.name: Cantor's set theory
events.summary: Cantor's study of exceptional sets for trigonometric series led to countability, uncountability of the reals, and then transfinite ordinals and cardinals.
keyWorks: Cantor, Ueber eine Eigenschaft des Inbegriffes aller reellen algebraischen Zahlen, Crelle 1874
Cantor, Grundlagen einer allgemeinen Mannigfaltigkeitslehre, 1883

evidence.paraphrase: Cantor moved from trigonometric uniqueness to uncountability of reals in 1873-74 and six Annalen papers in 1879-84.
Cantor's 1874 paper introduced cardinality via one-to-one correspondence and is treated as founding set theory.

W26.notes: Cantor, Crelle 77 (1874) and Math. Ann. 46/49 (1895-97) confirmed. Set theory born from the uniqueness problem for trigonometric series.

events.name: Erlangen programme
events.summary: Klein defined a geometry by the group of transformations leaving its properties invariant.
keyWorks: Klein, Vergleichende Betrachtungen ueber neuere geometrische Forschungen, 1872

evidence.paraphrase: Klein's 1872 programme characterized geometry via invariance under a transformation group.
Klein's 1872 programme tied geometry to its groups of symmetries.

M17.notes: Original Erlangen pamphlet 1872; Math. Ann. 43 reprint 1893 confirmed. Methodological date cannot precede 1872.

W3.notes: Klein's Erlangen programme (1872) confirmed. A dictionary between geometries and transformation groups.

events.name: Lie theory
events.summary: Lie combined contact transformations with integration theory of PDE to build continuous transformation groups and infinitesimal generators.
keyWorks: Lie, Theorie der Transformationsgruppen I-III, with Engel, 1888-93

evidence.paraphrase: Lie began systematic work on continuous groups in 1873-74, culminating in the three-volume Theorie.
Lie began systematic study of what are now called Lie groups from 1884, followed by Killing and Cartan.

W9.notes: Lie-Engel 1888-93 confirmed. Galois-style group ideas transferred to differential equations (Lie 1873-74).

events.name: Poincare's algebraic topology
events.summary: Poincare introduced homology and the fundamental group as algebraic invariants of manifolds.
keyWorks: Poincare, Analysis situs, J. Ecole Polytechnique 1895
Poincare, Complements a l'Analysis situs, 1899-1904

evidence.paraphrase: Analysis situs appeared in 1895 after a paper in 1894 introducing the fundamental group.
Poincare's 1895 Analysis Situs introduced ideas later called homotopy and homology.

M32.notes: Poincaré, J. Éc. Polytech. (2) 1 (1895) 1-121, which has no DOI; the citation is standard. 1895 is not an institutional date. DUPLICATE of W36: merge them.

W36.notes: DUPLICATE of M32: merge them. Source fields should be topology, algebra and analysis; 'geometry' is vague.

events.name: Commutative algebra from invariant theory and ideals
events.summary: Noether used chain conditions to treat primary decomposition and unique ideal factorization for abstract rings.
keyWorks: Noether, Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen, Math. Ann. 1921
Noether, Abstrakter Aufbau der Idealtheorie in algebraischen Zahl- und Funktionenkoerpern, 1926

evidence.paraphrase: Her 1921 paper decomposed ideals into primary ideals under the ascending chain condition.
Noether's 1921 paper introduced chain conditions, giving Noetherian rings.

M28.notes: Noether 1921 Math. Ann. 83 confirmed. The second paper appeared in Math. Ann. 96 in 1927 (received 1926). Overlaps W64 (same event); merge.

W64.notes: Lasker, Math. Ann. 60 (1905) and Noether 1921 confirmed. Same event as M28 (Macaulay 1913 is intermediate); merge.

events.name: Invariant theory and Hilbert basis theorem
events.summary: Gordan proved finite generation of binary invariants by hard computation, and Hilbert's abstract basis theorem settled the general case non-constructively, shifting algebra toward structure.
keyWorks: Gordan, Beweis, dass jede Covariante ... eine endliche Anzahl ... besitzt, 1868
Hilbert, Ueber die Theorie der algebraischen Formen, Math. Ann. 1890

evidence.paraphrase: Gordan proved finite generation in 1868 and Hilbert's thesis and basis theorem followed in 1885 and 1890.
In 1888 he proved his Basis Theorem, after his 1884 invariant thesis.

W62.notes: Gordan Crelle 69 (1868) and Hilbert Math. Ann. 36 (1890) confirmed. Abstract method settling invariant problem; conceptual 1840s Cayley-Boole roots out of scope. Duplicate of M25.

M25.notes: Duplicate of W62; Math. Ann. 36 (1890) confirmed.

events.name: Volterra functionals
events.summary: Volterra introduced functionals as functions of functions, and Hadamard named the field in 1910.
keyWorks: Volterra, Sopra le funzioni che dipendono da altre funzioni, 1887
Hadamard, Lecons sur le calcul des variations, 1910

evidence.paraphrase: The functional concept was introduced in 1887 by Volterra and the term was first used by Hadamard in 1910.
Volterra conceived the theory in 1883 and extended it in 1890.

W45.notes: Volterra 1887 Rend. Accad. Lincei note was not found in Crossref, though it is well attested; Hadamard 1910 Lecons confirmed. Duplicate of M41; merge.

M41.notes: Duplicate of W45; merge. 'Mechanics' as a source is weak: Volterra's hereditary mechanics comes after 1909.

events.name: Hilbert space and integral equations
from: quadratic forms in infinitely many variables
events.summary: Hilbert and Riesz made sequence and function spaces into an infinite-dimensional geometry with spectral theory.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Grundzuege einer allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen, 1904-1910
Riesz, Sur les systemes orthogonaux de fonctions, 1907

evidence.paraphrase: Hilbert's eigenvalue theory for Fredholm equations led directly to Hilbert spaces.
Volterra's 1887 functional concept preceded Hadamard's 1910 book, which founded the linear school.

M42.notes: Hilbert Goettinger Nachr. 1904-10 (Teubner reprint) confirmed; Riesz and Fischer 1907 CR notes, Schmidt 1908; book form 1912.

W44.notes: Acta Math. 27 (1903), doi 10.1007/bf02421317. Hilbert's Grundzüge (1912) is in Open Library; the Göttinger Nachrichten papers of 1904-10 are the methodological dates. A genuine fusion.

events.name: Banach spaces
events.summary: Banach defined complete normed spaces and proved the key theorems on operators, forming the Lwow school.
keyWorks: Banach, Sur les operations dans les ensembles abstraits, Fund. Math. 1922
Banach, Theorie des operations lineaires, 1932

evidence.paraphrase: Banach and Steinhaus first published the uniform boundedness principle in 1927.
His 1920 dissertation axiomatically defined Banach spaces.

W46.notes: Fund. Math. 3 (1922) and 1932 book confirmed; parallel Hahn and Wiener 1922.

M45.notes: Fund. Math. 3 (1922), doi 10.4064/fm-3-1-133-181. Théorie des opérations linéaires (1932) is in Open Library. Borderline as an internal abstraction. Hahn and Wiener (1922) were independent.

events.name: Metric spaces (Frechet)
events.summary: Frechet unified earlier function-space work by Cantor, Volterra, Arzela and Hadamard into abstract metric spaces.
keyWorks: Frechet, Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel, 1906

evidence.paraphrase: Frechet formalised the metric space in 1906, unifying earlier work on function spaces.
His 1906 dissertation introduced the metric space concept.

W40.notes: Rend. Palermo 22 (1906) confirmed; the name 'metric space' is Hausdorff 1914.

M43.notes: Frechet, Rend. Circ. Mat. Palermo 22 (1906) and Les espaces abstraits (1928) confirmed. The birth of abstract spaces fed general topology (Hausdorff 1914) and functional analysis.

events.name: Measure-theoretic probability
events.summary: Borel, Lebesgue, Kolmogorov applied measure theory to probability.
keyWorks: Kolmogorov, Grundbegriffe der Wahrscheinlichkeitsrechnung, 1933

evidence.paraphrase: The 1933 book builds probability axiomatically.

M74.notes: Kolmogorov 1933 confirmed; Borel 1909 Rend. Palermo and Wiener/Steinhaus 1923 give in-scope dates.

events.name: Lebesgue measure and integration
events.summary: Jordan, Borel and Lebesgue built measure on sets and defined an integral that behaves well under limits.
keyWorks: Borel, Lecons sur la theorie des fonctions, 1898
Lebesgue, Integrale, longueur, aire, 1902

evidence.paraphrase: Lebesgue published his integration theory in 1901.
His 1902 dissertation presents the major work on the integral.

W42.notes: Lebesgue 1902 Annali and Borel 1898 confirmed; Lebesgue 1901 CR note is the first statement.

M37.notes: Lebesgue, Annali di Mat. (3) 7 (1902), doi 10.1007/bf02420592, plus the CRAS note of 1901 and the Leçons of 1904. Fourier series was the application, not a source field. The 1898 conceptual date is Borel's measure, which is a precursor.

events.name: Group theory in quantum mechanics
events.summary: Symmetry groups of atoms and spectra are analysed by decomposing the state space into irreducible representations, which also drives the general theory.

events.name: Hilbert-space quantum mechanics
to: abstract Hilbert space and unbounded operator theory
events.summary: Matrix and wave mechanics were unified in the Hilbert-space framework by Weyl, Dirac and von Neumann.
keyWorks: Weyl, Gruppentheorie und Quantenmechanik, 1928
von Neumann, Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik, 1932

evidence.paraphrase: Von Neumann's 1932 book is credited with the first complete mathematical formulation.
He analysed the formal aspects in 1927-1929.

W75.notes: Genuine: von Neumann's axiomatic Hilbert space and the spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators (1927-29) are new mathematics prompted by physics. The key work should be von Neumann 1932 (Springer, in Open Library) together with Math. Ann. 102 (1929). Weyl 1928 belongs to M65.

M66.notes: von Neumann 1932 book confirmed; Hilbert, von Neumann and Nordheim, Math. Ann. 98 (1928, submitted 1927). Quantum physics fused with Hilbert-space theory.

events.name: Ergodic theory
events.summary: Boltzmann's ergodic hypothesis became a rigorous theorem when Birkhoff and von Neumann used Lebesgue measure and Hilbert space.
keyWorks: Birkhoff, Proof of the ergodic theorem, PNAS 1931
von Neumann, Proof of the quasi-ergodic hypothesis, 1932

evidence.paraphrase: The ergodic theorem made kinetic gas theory rigorous using Lebesgue measure.
Birkhoff's 1931 and von Neumann's 1932 papers established the ergodic theorems, motivated by statistical physics.

M36.notes: Birkhoff, PNAS 17 (1931) and von Neumann, PNAS 18 (1932) confirmed. Boltzmann's 1871 hypothesis puts the conceptual date in scope, but the methodological date (1931-32, with Koopman 1931) is just outside. Borderline.

W52.notes: Conceptual date in scope (Boltzmann 1871; Poincaré recurrence 1890). The theorems fall just after scope. PNAS 17 (1931), doi 10.1073/pnas.17.2.656, and PNAS 18 (1932), doi 10.1073/pnas.18.1.70. Koopman 1931 is the bridge and should be cited.

events.name: Number fields / function fields dictionary
events.summary: Dedekind and Weber applied ideal theory to function fields of Riemann surfaces, giving an algebraic proof of Riemann-Roch.
keyWorks: Dedekind and Weber, Theorie der algebraischen Functionen einer Veraenderlichen, Crelle 1882

evidence.paraphrase: The 1882 joint paper applied ideal theory to Riemann surfaces and proved Riemann-Roch algebraically.
Dedekind and Weber in 1882 gave a theory of algebraic function fields with a rigorous Riemann-Roch proof.

W21.notes: Crelle 92 (1882), doi 10.1515/crll.1882.92.181. Better typed as technique transfer, with a dictionary type also acceptable.

events.name: Game theory
events.summary: Zermelo, Borel and von Neumann treated games mathematically and proved minimax.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Zur Theorie der Gesellschaftsspiele, Math. Ann. 1928

evidence.paraphrase: Borel's minimax led him toward the subject.
Game theory's book-length genesis is the 1944 von Neumann-Morgenstern text, built on earlier fixed-point work.

M68.notes: von Neumann Math. Ann. 100 (1928) doi 10.1007/bf01448847. Games supply the idea, so import-from-outside.

W89.notes: von Neumann, Math. Ann. 100 (1928) confirmed. Zermelo (ICM 1912, printed 1913) and Borel 1921 count as conceptual. Imported from parlour games and economics. The topology tie is weak in 1928.

events.name: Riemann zeta and prime number theorem
events.summary: Riemann treated the prime-counting problem through the zeta function as a complex-analytic object, opening a path from complex analysis to the distribution of primes.
keyWorks: Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Groesse, 1859

evidence.paraphrase: Riemann's 1859 paper studied the zeta function as a complex function and stated the Riemann hypothesis.
Hadamard proved the theorem in 1896 by complex analysis, independently of de la Vallee Poussin.
Riemann's 1859 zeta work is the canonical start of complex-analytic methods.

M3.notes: Riemann 1859 Monatsberichte Berlin (Crossref has Werke reprint). Genuine complex analysis to primes transfer; overlaps M4.

M4.notes: Hadamard Bull. SMF 24 (1896) confirmed; de la Vallee Poussin Ann. Soc. Sci. Bruxelles 20 (1896). Settles Riemann's programme; overlaps M3.

W17.notes: Hadamard, Bull. SMF 24 (1896), doi 10.24033/bsmf.545. Riemann's paper is in Monatsber. Berlin 1859 (no DOI). De la Vallée Poussin's paper appeared the same year. Landau 1909 is the institutional date.

events.name: Circle method
events.summary: Hardy, Ramanujan and Littlewood used contour integrals to count partitions and Waring representations.
keyWorks: Hardy and Ramanujan, Asymptotic formulae in combinatory analysis, 1918
Hardy and Littlewood, Partitio numerorum, 1920-28

evidence.paraphrase: The Partitio numerorum used the Hardy-Littlewood-Ramanujan method.

events.name: Brownian motion
events.summary: Bachelier, Einstein and Smoluchowski modelled random motion probabilistically, and Wiener later gave it a rigorous measure.
keyWorks: Bachelier, Theorie de la speculation, 1900
Einstein, Ueber die von der molekularkinetischen Theorie ... geforderte Bewegung, Ann. Phys. 1905
Wiener, Differential-space, 1923

evidence.paraphrase: The article places Brownian motion and Markov processes in twentieth-century probability.

W54.notes: Ann. ENS 17 (1900), doi 10.24033/asens.476. Ann. Phys. 322 (1905), doi 10.1002/andp.19053220806. J. Math. Phys. 2 (1923), doi 10.1002/sapm192321131. A genuine import from outside.

events.name: Automorphic functions and uniformisation
events.summary: Poincare and Klein linked discrete groups of Mobius transformations, hyperbolic geometry and differential equations, and uniformised algebraic curves.
keyWorks: Poincare, Theorie des groupes fuchsiens, Acta Math. 1882
Klein and Fricke, Vorlesungen ueber die Theorie der automorphen Functionen, 1897-1912

evidence.paraphrase: Discrete groups were developed by Klein, Lie, Poincare and Picard, connected to modular forms and monodromy.
Poincare began publishing in 1881 and the two raced to a uniformization theorem.

W76.notes: Poincare, Acta Math. 1 (1882) and Klein-Fricke vols 1897-1912 confirmed. Fuchsian groups identified with hyperbolic isometries, combining complex analysis, ODEs, group theory and non-Euclidean geometry. Uniformisation itself dates to Poincare and Koebe 1907.

M33.notes: Acta Math. 1 (1882), doi 10.1007/bf02592124. Klein's Ikosaeder (1884) exists but is the wrong key work. Use Klein, Math. Ann. 21 (1883) and the Poincaré-Klein correspondence. Institutional: the Fricke-Klein Vorlesungen of 1897-1912, not 1884. Uniformization itself came in 1907 (Koebe, Poincaré).

events.name: Dynamical systems from celestial mechanics
events.summary: Poincare studied orbits geometrically rather than by formulae, uncovering homoclinic phenomena in the three-body problem, and Birkhoff built on this.
keyWorks: Poincare, Sur les courbes definies par une equation differentielle, 1881-86
Poincare, Les methodes nouvelles de la mecanique celeste, 1892-99
Birkhoff, Dynamical Systems, 1927

evidence.paraphrase: Poincare's recurrence theorem was the first result about long-run behaviour of dynamical systems.
His prize memoir was revised in 1890 and the three-volume Methodes nouvelles followed.

W50.notes: Birkhoff 1927 and Methodes nouvelles 1892-99 confirmed; Poincare 1881-86 J. Math. Pures Appl. Duplicate of M34.

M34.notes: Methodes nouvelles 1892 confirmed; Acta Math. 13 (1890) not matched by Crossref query. Duplicate of W50.

events.name: Lyapunov stability
events.summary: Lyapunov gave general criteria for stability of equilibria using auxiliary functions.
keyWorks: Lyapunov, The General Problem of the Stability of Motion, 1892

evidence.paraphrase: Dynamical systems theory began in Newtonian mechanics, with general solutions only for small classes.
His 1892 thesis was fundamental to stability of critical points.

W51.notes: Lyapunov's 1892 Kharkov thesis confirmed (1992 English translation). Stability theory as a field, from mechanics and ODEs. Duplicate of M35.

events.name: Geometry of numbers
events.summary: Minkowski used convex bodies to attack Diophantine and quadratic form problems.
keyWorks: Minkowski, Geometrie der Zahlen, 1896-1910

evidence.paraphrase: He initiated it in 1890.
Minkowski presented his Geometry of Numbers in 1896.

M69.notes: Minkowski, Crelle 107 (1891) and Geometrie der Zahlen (1896) confirmed. Duplicate of W18.

W18.notes: Duplicate of M69; merge. This is a fusion of convex geometry and number theory, not an import from outside.

events.name: Boolean algebra of logic
events.summary: Boole, Peirce and Schroeder treated logic as an algebra of classes and relations.
keyWorks: Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought, 1854
Schroeder, Vorlesungen ueber die Algebra der Logik, 1890-95

evidence.paraphrase: Boole was first to present logic as a mathematical theory in algebraic style.

M48.notes: Boole 1854 and Schroeder 1890-95 confirmed. Boole's first work is 1847 (pre-scope), but Laws of Thought 1854 and Peirce 1870 fall in scope. Fusion of algebra and logic.

events.name: Markov chains
events.summary: Markov studied dependent trials and showed the law of large numbers extends to chains, later applying them to letter sequences.
keyWorks: Markov, Extension of the law of large numbers to dependent quantities, 1906

evidence.paraphrase: Markov processes belong to twentieth-century probability.
After 1900 he applied Chebyshev's methods to chains.

W55.notes: Markov 1906 Izv. Fiz.-Mat. Obshch. Kazan (not in Crossref); 1913 Onegin letter-chain study correct. Duplicate of M72.

M72.notes: Duplicate of W55; continued fractions source is doubtful.

events.name: Hilbert's programme
events.summary: Hilbert proposed to prove consistency of mathematics by finitary methods.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Axiomatisches Denken, 1918
Hilbert and Ackermann, Grundzuege der theoretischen Logik, 1928

evidence.paraphrase: He made consistency of analysis his second problem in 1900.
The metamathematical period from 1910 is associated with Hilbert's finitist system.

M54.notes: Hilbert-Ackermann 1928 confirmed (Open Library); Axiomatisches Denken Math. Ann. 78 (1918). Conceptual start better 1904 Heidelberg lecture. Duplicate of W33.

W33.notes: Duplicate of M54; Hilbert-Ackermann 1928 confirmed. Mathematische Probleme 1900 is a weak anchor for proof theory.

events.name: Cartan exterior differential calculus
events.summary: Cartan developed the exterior derivative and used it with Pfaffian systems and moving frames to unify differential geometry with Lie theory.
keyWorks: Cartan, Sur certaines expressions differentielles et le probleme de Pfaff, 1899
Cartan, Lecons sur les invariants integraux, 1922

evidence.paraphrase: Cartan developed the exterior derivative in 1901.
The 1899 paper gave the first formal definition of a differential form.

W85.notes: Cartan 1899 Ann. ENS (doi 10.24033/asens.467) and 1922 Lecons confirmed. Duplicate of M23.

M23.notes: Duplicate of W85; Ann. ENS 1899 confirmed. Methodological start cannot precede 1899.

events.name: Affine connections (Levi-Civita, Weyl)
events.summary: Levi-Civita introduced parallel transport, Weyl generalised to gauge geometry, and Cartan developed connections and moving frames.
keyWorks: Levi-Civita, Nozione di parallelismo in una varieta qualunque, 1917
Weyl, Gravitation und Elektrizitaet, 1918

evidence.paraphrase: Levi-Civita encouraged general covariance in Einstein's work and Weyl contributed in 1917.
Weyl's 1918 book introduced gauge-type ideas.

W93.notes: Levi-Civita Rend. Palermo 42 (1917; Crossref dates 1916) confirmed.

M60.notes: Levi-Civita, Rend. Palermo 42 (published Dec 1916), doi 10.1007/bf03014898. Weyl, Math. Z. 2 (1918), doi 10.1007/bf01199420. Cartan, Ann. ENS 40 (1923), doi 10.24033/asens.751. Physics supplied the idea.

events.name: Arithmetization and construction of the reals
events.summary: Weierstrass, Cantor and Dedekind defined real numbers from rationals via limits or cuts, removing reliance on geometric intuition.
keyWorks: Dedekind, Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen, 1872
Cantor, Ueber die Ausdehnung eines Satzes aus der Theorie der trigonometrischen Reihen, Math. Ann. 1872

evidence.paraphrase: Dedekind's cut idea of 1858 was published in 1872, the same year Cantor gave a sequence definition.
Dedekind built the real numbers using cuts in 1871-72.

M6.notes: Arithmetization of analysis (Weierstrass lectures 1860s, Dedekind cuts 1858/1872, Cantor 1872 Math. Ann. 5). Logic is not really a source field. Duplicate of W25.

events.name: Frege predicate logic
events.summary: Frege invented quantified predicate logic and tried to derive arithmetic from it.
keyWorks: Frege, Begriffsschrift, 1879
Frege, Grundgesetze der Arithmetik, 1893-1903

evidence.paraphrase: The logicist period begins with Frege's Begriffsschrift and ends with Principia Mathematica.
The Begriffsschrift of 1879 contains the first predicate calculus.

M49.notes: Begriffsschrift 1879 and Grundgesetze 1893 confirmed. Quantificational logic built to formalise arithmetic: a fusion of logic and mathematics.

events.name: Peano arithmetic axioms
events.summary: Dedekind and Peano gave axioms characterizing the natural numbers, Peano in formal logical notation.
keyWorks: Dedekind, Was sind und was sollen die Zahlen, 1888
Peano, Arithmetices principia, 1889

evidence.paraphrase: Peano's 1889 booklet set out the axioms.
Around 1900 Peano helped develop his axioms using set-theoretic ideas and introduced the membership symbol.

M50.notes: Dedekind 1888 confirmed (Open Library); Peano 1889 Turin, Bocca (not in Crossref).

W31.notes: Arithmetices principia 1889 confirmed; Formulario 1895-1908. The symbolic-logic axiomatisation of arithmetic is a reification. Dedekind's 'Was sind und was sollen die Zahlen?' (1888) is the conceptual twin and should be added.

events.name: Biometric mathematical statistics
events.summary: Pearson developed correlation and chi-square for biological data and founded Biometrika.
keyWorks: Pearson, Mathematical Contributions to the Theory of Evolution, 1893-1912

evidence.paraphrase: Eighteen papers 1893-1912; chi-square 1900.
Pearson developed chi distance, p-values and PCA around 1900, founded Biometrika, and a statistics department in 1911.

M75.notes: First paper is 'Contributions to the Mathematical Theory of Evolution', Phil. Trans. A 1894; later parts titled 'Mathematical Contributions...'; chi-square Phil. Mag. 1900 confirmed.

W58.notes: Natural Inheritance (1889) is in Open Library. Pearson, Phil. Mag. (5) 50 (1900), doi 10.1080/14786440009463897. Galton's reversion and regression work starts in 1877 and 1885. Biometrika (1901) and UCL Applied Statistics (1911) mark the institutional dates.

events.name: Fisher statistical inference
events.summary: Fisher unified chi-squared, small-sample t and variance analysis into a framework tested on Rothamsted crop data.
keyWorks: Fisher, The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance, 1918
Fisher, Statistical Methods for Research Workers, 1925
Fisher, The Design of Experiments, 1935

evidence.paraphrase: Fisher in 1924 combined chi-squared and t in one framework and published a handbook in 1925.
He introduced likelihood in 1921.

W59.notes: Fisher Trans. RSE 52 (1918, Crossref 1919) and 1925 book confirmed.

M76.notes: Borderline. The likelihood and sufficiency programme (Phil. Trans. A 222, 1922) is internal to statistics. Design of experiments and ANOVA, out of Rothamsted agriculture, is a genuine new area. Statistical Methods for Research Workers (1925) is in Open Library.

events.name: Killing-Cartan classification
events.summary: Killing and Cartan decomposed semisimple Lie algebras into simple ones and classified them into four families plus exceptional cases.
keyWorks: Killing, Die Zusammensetzung der stetigen endlichen Transformationsgruppen, Math. Ann. 1888-90
Cartan, thesis, 1894

evidence.paraphrase: Killing and Cartan showed semisimple Lie algebras split into simple ones and classified them.

W10.notes: Killing Math. Ann. 31-36 (1888-90) confirmed; Cartan thesis 1894. Borderline internal to Lie theory but Lie algebras become objects in their own right.

events.name: General topology (Hausdorff)
events.summary: Hausdorff's Grundzuege gave neighborhood axioms for topological spaces.
keyWorks: Hausdorff, Grundzuege der Mengenlehre, 1914

evidence.paraphrase: The 1914 book develops topological and metric spaces.
Hausdorff coined topological space in 1914 and Kuratowski gave the modern definition in 1922.

W41.notes: Hausdorff's Grundzüge (1914) is in Open Library. Fund. Math. 3 (1922), doi 10.4064/fm-3-1-182-199. Reification of point-set topology. Fréchet's 1906 thesis is a precursor.

events.name: Vector analysis
events.summary: Gibbs and Heaviside extracted vector methods from quaternions.
keyWorks: Gibbs, Elements of Vector Analysis, 1881-84; Wilson, Vector Analysis, 1901

evidence.paraphrase: Gibbs wrote notes in 1881 and 1884.
Quaternions were discovered in 1843 and Stokes proved his theorem in 1850.

M77.notes: Gibbs 1881 privately printed (Smithsonian scan) and Wilson 1901 confirmed.

W86.notes: The name is misleading: Stokes and Green are not the event; it is Gibbs and Heaviside splitting vectors from quaternions. Gibbs's Elements were privately printed (no record). Gibbs-Wilson 1901 is in Open Library.

events.name: Italian algebraic geometry
events.summary: Castelnuovo, Enriques and Severi classified algebraic surfaces up to birational equivalence with geometric methods lacking rigorous foundations.
keyWorks: Castelnuovo and Enriques, Sulle condizioni di razionalita dei piani doppi, 1896
Enriques, Introduzione alla geometria sopra le superficie algebriche, 1896

evidence.paraphrase: The Italian school classified surfaces up to birational isomorphism using generic points without precise definition.

W83.notes: Castelnuovo-Enriques piani doppi is Rend. Palermo 14 (1900), not 1896; Enriques 1896 Introduzione is a memoir (Mem. Soc. Ital. Sci.). Borderline internal to algebraic geometry.

events.name: Model theory beginnings
events.summary: Loewenheim and Skolem showed that first-order theories with infinite models have countable ones, opening semantic study of formal theories.
keyWorks: Loewenheim, Ueber Moeglichkeiten im Relativkalkuel, Math. Ann. 1915
Skolem, Logisch-kombinatorische Untersuchungen, 1920

evidence.paraphrase: Loewenheim and Skolem worked in a non-finitist metamathematical system.
Hilbert 1899 built models where the parallel postulate fails.

W32.notes: Loewenheim Math. Ann. 76 (1915) confirmed; Skolem 1920 Videnskapsselskapets Skrifter.

M55.notes: Math. Ann. 76 (1915), doi 10.1007/bf01458217. Monatsh. 37 (1930), doi 10.1007/bf01696781. Skolem 1920 needs a full citation. Hilbert 1899 is a precursor, not the conceptual date.

events.name: Axiomatic set theory (Zermelo)
events.summary: Zermelo proved well-ordering from choice and axiomatized set theory.
keyWorks: Zermelo, Beweis dass jede Menge wohlgeordnet werden kann, 1904
Zermelo, Untersuchungen ueber die Grundlagen der Mengenlehre I, 1908

evidence.paraphrase: Zermelo gave well-ordering in 1904 and axioms in 1908.
Zermelo, Fraenkel and others proposed axiom systems to eliminate paradoxes and von Neumann gave one in 1925.

M53.notes: Zermelo Math. Ann. 59 (1904) and 65 (1908) confirmed. Axiomatics applied to set theory after paradoxes.

W27.notes: Math. Ann. 65 (1908), doi 10.1007/bf01449999. Crelle 154 (1925), doi 10.1515/crll.1925.154.219. Reification is a fair type.

events.name: Minkowski spacetime
events.summary: Minkowski reformulated special relativity as geometry of four dimensions.
keyWorks: Minkowski, Raum und Zeit, 1909

evidence.paraphrase: He reformulated Einstein's paper in 1908.

M62.notes: Raum und Zeit 1909 confirmed; Goettinger Nachr. 1908 paper precedes. Borderline physics-led.

events.name: Abstract group concept
events.summary: Cayley, Kronecker, Weber and von Dyck gradually axiomatised groups independently of permutations, ending with the full modern definition.
keyWorks: Cayley, On the theory of groups, Phil. Mag. 1854
von Dyck, Gruppentheoretische Studien, Math. Ann. 1882
Schmidt, Abstract Theory of Groups, 1916

evidence.paraphrase: Von Dyck in 1882 first required inverses, and Schmidt's 1916 book treated finite and infinite abstract groups.
In 1854 Cayley defined an abstract group and gave multiplication tables.

W8.notes: Cayley Phil. Mag. 1854 and von Dyck Math. Ann. 20 (1882) confirmed; Schmidt 1916 Kiev Russian original.

M15.notes: Cayley, Phil. Mag. 7 (1854) confirmed. Little uptake until Cayley 1878 and Dyck 1882; Weber 1893-96 is institutional.

events.name: Brouwer topology
events.summary: Brouwer used simplicial approximation and degree to prove invariance of dimension and the fixed-point theorem.
keyWorks: Brouwer, Beweis der Invarianz der Dimensionszahl, Math. Ann. 1911
Brouwer, Ueber Abbildung von Mannigfaltigkeiten, Math. Ann. 1912

evidence.paraphrase: Brouwer presented his fixed-point theorem in 1912.
Most of his topology work dates 1909-1913.

W39.notes: Combinatorial (simplicial) methods settle Cantor-era point-set question of dimension invariance. Exact title is 'Beweis der Invarianz der Dimensionenzahl', Math. Ann. 70 (1911); 'Ueber Abbildung von Mannigfaltigkeiten' Math. Ann. 71 (1911/12). Duplicate of M46.

M46.notes: Duplicate of W39; merge. Dates 1909-13 are fine.

events.name: Noether's theorem
events.summary: Noether tied continuous symmetries of an action to conserved quantities, answering questions in general relativity.
keyWorks: Noether, Invariante Variationsprobleme, Nachr. Goettingen 1918

evidence.paraphrase: Her work on invariant variational problems linked symmetries to conservation laws.
Noether proved in 1915 a theorem linking physical symmetries to conservation laws.

M30.notes: Lie-group invariance plus variational calculus yields conservation laws, answering the energy-conservation question in general relativity; Nachr. Ges. Wiss. Goettingen 1918 (confirmed via Gesammelte Abhandlungen). Duplicate of W73.

W73.notes: Duplicate of M30. Better typed as technique transfer than dictionary.

events.name: Representation theory of finite groups
events.summary: Frobenius, Burnside and Schur studied groups through matrix representations, and character tables proved structural theorems such as Burnside's p^a q^b.
keyWorks: Frobenius, Ueber Gruppencharaktere, 1896
Burnside, On the theory of groups of finite order, 1897; Theory of Groups of Finite Order, 1897
Schur, Neue Begruendung der Theorie der Gruppencharaktere, 1905

evidence.paraphrase: Burnside, Frobenius and Molien developed representation theory of finite groups in the late 1800s.
The page treats 1897 as the birth year of representation theory, building on letters to Dedekind.

W67.notes: Frobenius 1896 (Sitzungsber. Berlin; not in Crossref but well attested), Burnside book 1897 and Schur 1905 confirmed. Burnside's p^a q^b theorem is 1904. This is a fusion of group theory and linear algebra, not a dictionary.

M20.notes: Genuine birth of representation theory, out of Dedekind's group determinant. Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. 1896, pp. 985-1021, and 1897. No DOI. Burnside's 2nd edition (1911) is a good institutional marker.

events.name: Matrix algebra
events.summary: Sylvester named matrices and Cayley gave their algebra, with product and inverse.
keyWorks: Cayley, A memoir on the theory of matrices, Phil. Trans. 1858
Sylvester, Additions to the articles on a new class of theorems, Phil. Mag. 1850

evidence.paraphrase: Cayley's 1855 and 1858 papers introduced matrix inversion and multiplication.
Cayley worked on matrix algebras in 1855 and 1858.

M24.notes: Cayley, Phil. Trans. 148 (1858) and Sylvester, Phil. Mag. 37 (1850) confirmed. Matrix algebra was abstracted from determinants and linear substitutions.

W14.notes: Phil. Trans. 148 (1858), doi 10.1098/rstl.1858.0002. Frobenius, Crelle 84 (1878), doi 10.1515/crll.1878.84.1. Arguably an internal algebra advance, but defensible as abstraction.

events.name: Class field theory
events.summary: Abelian extensions of number fields were matched to ideal-class-type groups, from Kronecker, Weber and Hilbert through Takagi's existence theorem and Artin's reciprocity law.
keyWorks: Takagi, Ueber eine Theorie des relativ Abel'schen Zahlkoerpers, 1920
Artin, Beweis des allgemeinen Reziprozitaetsgesetzes, 1927

evidence.paraphrase: The Takagi existence theorem was known by 1920 and Artin's reciprocity law became the central formulation.
Artin's 1927 law included all previously known reciprocity laws and extended Takagi's 1920 theory.

W20.notes: Takagi 1920 (J. Coll. Sci. Tokyo) and Artin, Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 5 (1927) confirmed. A dictionary between abelian extensions and generalised ideal class groups. Duplicate of M13.

M13.notes: Duplicate of W20; merge. Artin 1927 confirmed. Hasse's Bericht (Jahresber. DMV, 1926-30) is institutional. The core is a dictionary, with L-series (Weber, Dirichlet density) as a tool.

events.name: Heaviside operational calculus
events.summary: Heaviside treated differentiation as an algebraic operator to solve telegraph and circuit equations, later justified through Laplace transforms.
keyWorks: Heaviside, Electromagnetic Theory, 1893-1912

evidence.paraphrase: Arbogast in 1800 first separated operation symbols from quantities, and Boole used the methods freely.
Developed 1880-1887.

W92.notes: Heaviside, Electromagnetic Theory vol. 1 (1893) confirmed. Imported from engineering; justified by Bromwich (1916) and Carson (1922) via Laplace and contour integrals.

M78.notes: A genuine import from engineering. Electrical Papers (1892) is in Open Library, but the operational calculus is developed most fully in Electromagnetic Theory vol. 2 (1899) and the Proc. Roy. Soc. papers of 1893. Rigour came from Bromwich (1916) and Carson (1926).

events.name: Axiomatisation of geometry
events.summary: Hilbert gave a complete independent axiom system for Euclidean geometry that did not rely on diagrams, and used models to test independence.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Grundlagen der Geometrie, 1899

evidence.paraphrase: In 1899 Hilbert presented a self-consistent set of geometric axioms.
Pasch's 1882 lectures and Hilbert's 1899 book set higher standards of axiomatization.

W6.notes: Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899 Festschrift) confirmed. Independence and consistency proofs by arithmetic models make the axiomatic method an object of study. Pasch 1882 is a precursor.

M31.notes: The axiomatic method becomes an object in its own right: independence is shown through models. This is closer to reification than to abstraction. Pasch 1882 and Hilbert 1899 are both in Open Library (Hilbert's first edition appeared in the Gauss-Weber Festschrift). It overlaps with W2, which supplies the model technique.

events.name: Intuitionism
events.summary: Brouwer rejected the unrestricted law of excluded middle.
keyWorks: Brouwer, Over de Grondslagen der Wiskunde, thesis 1907
Heyting, Die formalen Regeln der intuitionistischen Logik, 1930

evidence.paraphrase: His 1907 dissertation began intuitionism, and 1908 rejected excluded middle.
Weyl and Brouwer were later opponents of the classical set-theoretic approach.

M47.notes: Brouwer's thesis (1907) confirmed; Heyting 1930 (Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad.) not in Crossref but well attested. Philosophy is not quite an 'outside' source in the overview's sense. Better seen as a foundational birth, yielding intuitionistic logic.

W34.notes: Brouwer's thesis (1907) and the 1908 paper in Tijdschrift voor Wijsbegeerte are standard citations; Crossref has no record. Heyting's formalisation of intuitionistic logic (1930) is the clearer methodological endpoint. Topology is not a source field.

events.name: p-adic numbers
events.summary: Hensel treated integers like power series in a prime, giving p-adic numbers, and Kuerschak and Hasse later turned this into valuation theory and local-global principles.
keyWorks: Hensel, Ueber eine neue Begruendung der Theorie der algebraischen Zahlen, 1899
Hensel, Theorie der algebraischen Zahlen, 1908

evidence.paraphrase: Hensel first described p-adic numbers in 1897.
Weierstrass's power-series method led Hensel to invent p-adic numbers in 1897.

W19.notes: Hensel's 1897 note appeared in Jahresber. DMV 6 (printed 1899); Crossref also shows a Crelle 128 (1905) paper with the same title. The 1908 book is confirmed. This rests on the analogy between number fields and function fields (power series at a point). Valuations: Kurschak 1913; local-global: Hasse 1921-23.

M11.notes: A genuine dictionary transfer from Riemann surfaces to number fields. The 1897 announcement is Jahresber. DMV 6 (not found in Crossref). Theorie der algebraischen Zahlen (1908) is in Open Library.

events.name: Ramsey theory
events.summary: Ramsey proved a combinatorial theorem on homogeneous subsets while studying a decision problem in logic, and van der Waerden proved a related Ramsey-type theorem on arithmetic progressions.
keyWorks: Ramsey, On a problem of formal logic, Proc. LMS 1930
van der Waerden, Beweis einer Baudetschen Vermutung, 1927

evidence.paraphrase: Ramsey's theorem arose from a problem in formal logic.
Read in 1928 and published 1930.

W88.notes: Proc. LMS s2-30 (1930), doi 10.1112/plms/s2-30.1.264, read in 1928. The direction is reversed: Ramsey built a combinatorial lemma as a tool for logic. Ramsey theory as a field forms later (Erdős-Szekeres 1935). Van der Waerden 1927 is independent and not Ramsey-derived. DUPLICATE of M82: merge them.

M82.notes: DUPLICATE of W88: merge them. Proc. LMS (1930), doi 10.1112/plms/s2-30.1.264.

events.name: Functional analysis
events.summary: Integral equations and the calculus of variations are treated as linear algebra in infinite-dimensional normed spaces with topological structure.

events.name: Distributions: from Dirac's delta to generalised functions
events.summary: Objects used formally by physicists (the delta function) are given a rigorous home as continuous functionals on test functions, which becomes the basis of modern PDE.

events.name: Deriving the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics
events.summary: Hilbert's sixth-problem programme of deriving kinetic equations from Newtonian particle systems is carried to long times for hard spheres.

events.name: Representations of compact and continuous groups (Schur, Weyl, Peter-Weyl)
events.summary: Schur and Weyl used invariant integration to extend finite-group representation theory to compact Lie groups.
keyWorks: Weyl, Theorie der Darstellung kontinuierlicher halbeinfacher Gruppen, Math. Z. 1925-26
Peter and Weyl, Die Vollstaendigkeit der primitiven Darstellungen, 1927

evidence.paraphrase: The Peter-Weyl theorem is cited from 1927 as showing irreducible unitary representations of compact groups are finite-dimensional.

W68.notes: Weyl Math. Z. 1925-26 and Peter-Weyl Math. Ann. 1927 confirmed; Hurwitz 1897 and Schur 1924 invariant integration are the conceptual roots.

events.name: Weyl's gauge theory
events.summary: Weyl proposed local scale invariance.
keyWorks: Weyl, Gravitation und Elektrizitaet, 1918

evidence.paraphrase: Raum-Zeit-Materie 1918 introduced a gauge-type idea.

M64.notes: Weyl 1918 Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. (Crossref shows reprints); 1929 Z. Phys. U(1) phase version. Borderline physics-led; keep as import with low weight.

events.name: Geometric (Clifford) algebra
events.summary: Clifford fused Hamilton's quaternions and Grassmann's exterior algebra into a single geometric algebra.
keyWorks: Clifford, Applications of Grassmann's Extensive Algebra, Am. J. Math. 1878

evidence.paraphrase: Clifford in 1878 unified quaternions with Grassmann's algebra.

W13.notes: Am. J. Math. 1 (1878) doi 10.2307/2369379. Methodological end 1930 is arbitrary; Lipschitz 1880-86 continued it.

events.name: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and algebraic geometry as ideal theory
events.summary: Hilbert linked ideals of polynomials to geometric zero sets, starting the algebraisation of algebraic geometry.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Ueber die vollen Invariantensysteme, Math. Ann. 1893

evidence.paraphrase: Hilbert's basis theorem and Nullstellensatz began the algebraization of algebraic geometry through commutative algebra.

events.name: Homology groups (Noether) and algebraic topology
events.summary: Noether's insight that Betti numbers are ranks of groups moved topology toward group-valued invariants, and the field was renamed accordingly.
keyWorks: Hopf, Eine Verallgemeinerung der Euler-Poincareschen Formel, 1928
Lefschetz, Algebraic Topology, 1942

evidence.paraphrase: In the 1920s and 30s emphasis grew on associating algebraic groups to spaces, leading to the new name.

W38.notes: Hopf 1928 confirmed via reprints, Alexandroff-Hopf 1935; Noether 1925 lectures, Vietoris 1926. Lefschetz 1942 is the renaming.

events.name: Rigorous foundations of algebraic geometry via commutative algebra
events.summary: Van der Waerden, Zariski and Weil used valuation and ideal theory to rebuild the Italian school's results rigorously.
keyWorks: van der Waerden, Zur algebraischen Geometrie I-III, Math. Ann. 1933-
Zariski, Algebraic Surfaces, 1935

evidence.paraphrase: Van der Waerden, Zariski and Weil gave a precise definition of generic point in the 1930s.

W84.notes: van der Waerden Math. Ann. 1933 series and Zariski 1935 confirmed; in-scope anchor is van der Waerden 1926 generic points paper.

events.name: Structure of associative algebras (Wedderburn)
events.summary: Cartan, Frobenius and Molien decomposed algebras over C, and Wedderburn extended this to arbitrary fields.
keyWorks: Wedderburn, On Hypercomplex Numbers, Proc. LMS 1907

evidence.paraphrase: Wedderburn in 1907 extended the decomposition results to arbitrary fields.

W66.notes: Wedderburn PLMS (2) 6 appeared 1908 (doi 10.1112/plms/s2-6.1.77), read 1907; Molien 1893 and Cartan 1898 precede.

events.name: Betti numbers and early combinatorial topology
events.summary: Riemann's connectivity of surfaces was extended by Betti to higher-dimensional spaces via numerical invariants.
keyWorks: Betti, Sopra gli spazi di un numero qualunque di dimensioni, 1871

evidence.paraphrase: Late nineteenth-century contributors to topology include Cauchy, Schlaefli, Riemann and Betti.

W37.notes: Betti Annali (2) 4 dated 1870-71 in Crossref; Poincare Analysis situs 1895.

events.name: Transcendence proofs for e and pi
events.summary: Liouville, Hermite and Lindemann used analytic constructions to show specific numbers are not algebraic, settling squaring the circle.
keyWorks: Hermite, Sur la fonction exponentielle, 1873
Lindemann, Ueber die Zahl pi, Math. Ann. 1882

evidence.paraphrase: Hermite proved e transcendental in 1873 and Lindemann did so for pi in 1882.

W94.notes: Lindemann Math. Ann. 20 (1882) confirmed; Hermite CR 77 (1873). Liouville 1844 precursor out of scope.

events.name: Differential Galois theory
events.summary: Picard and Vessiot carried the Galois correspondence to linear differential equations, with Lie groups replacing finite groups.
keyWorks: Picard, Sur les equations differentielles lineaires, 1883
Vessiot, Sur la theorie de Galois et ses diverses generalisations, 1904

evidence.paraphrase: Abel and Liouville asked which differential equations integrate in finite form.

W79.notes: Picard 1887 Ann. Toulouse and Vessiot 1904 Ann. ENS confirmed; Picard 1883 CR note first.

events.name: Russell paradox, type theory and Principia Mathematica
events.summary: Russell's paradox led to the ramified theory of types and the formal derivation of mathematics.
keyWorks: Russell, The Principles of Mathematics, 1903
Whitehead and Russell, Principia Mathematica, 1910-13

evidence.paraphrase: Russell found the paradox in 1901 and published the types in 1908.

M52.notes: Type theory born to block Russell's paradox; key methodological work is Russell, 'Mathematical logic as based on the theory of types', Am. J. Math. 30 (1908), confirmed. PM 1910-13 and Principles 1903 confirmed. Philosophy is not a needed source field.

events.name: Steinitz abstract field theory
events.summary: Steinitz gave the first abstract definition of field and proved every field has an algebraic closure.
keyWorks: Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Koerper, Crelle 1910

evidence.paraphrase: The 1910 paper gave the first abstract field definition and algebraic closures.

M27.notes: Steinitz, Crelle 137 (1910) confirmed. Abstracted from number fields, function fields, Galois fields and Hensel's p-adics. Overlaps W65.

events.name: Calculus of variations to Hilbert's direct methods
events.summary: Hilbert justified Dirichlet's principle with direct variational methods, rescuing Riemann's use of minimisation in complex analysis.
keyWorks: Hilbert, Ueber das Dirichletsche Princip, 1900

evidence.paraphrase: Hilbert justified Riemann's Dirichlet principle in 1900.

W47.notes: Hilbert, Jahresber. DMV 8 (1900) confirmed via Gesammelte Abhandlungen. The direct method rescues Riemann's existence proofs in function theory. Borderline: much of this is internal to the calculus of variations.

events.name: Fredholm integral equations
events.summary: Fredholm treated integral equations as limits of linear algebraic systems and solved the Dirichlet problem.
keyWorks: Fredholm, Sur une nouvelle methode pour la resolution du probleme de Dirichlet, 1900
Fredholm, Sur une classe d'equations fonctionnelles, Acta Math. 1903

evidence.paraphrase: 1900 preliminary report, fuller 1903 version.

M40.notes: Fredholm, Acta Math. 27 (1903) confirmed; the 1900 note is in Ofversigt Kongl. Vetenskaps-Akad. Forh. 57. Determinant theory carried over to integral equations and the Dirichlet problem.

events.name: Borel sets and measure
events.summary: Borel introduced a hierarchy of sets generated from open sets and applied countable additivity.
keyWorks: Borel, Lecons sur la theorie des fonctions, 1898

evidence.paraphrase: He introduced Borel sets in 1898.

M38.notes: Borel's Lecons 1898 confirmed. Lebesgue's 'Integrale, longueur, aire' (Annali 1902), also confirmed, is the methodological date. Fusion of Cantorian set theory and real analysis.

events.name: Many-valued logics
events.summary: Lukasiewicz and Post independently defined logics with more than two truth values.
keyWorks: Lukasiewicz, O logice trojwartosciowej, 1920
Post, Introduction to a general theory of elementary propositions, Am. J. Math. 1921

evidence.paraphrase: Metamathematical-era logic developed several new systems including those of Post and Lukasiewicz.

W35.notes: Post, Am. J. Math. 43 (1921) confirmed; Lukasiewicz 1920 (Ruch Filozoficzny 5) is not in Crossref. A new subfield of logic, but single-field, so borderline.

events.name: Godel's completeness and incompleteness theorems
events.summary: Godel arithmetized syntax inside number theory to show undecidable sentences.
keyWorks: Godel, Die Vollstaendigkeit der Axiome des logischen Funktionenkalkuels, 1930
Godel, Ueber formal unentscheidbare Saetze, 1931

evidence.paraphrase: Completeness in 1929 and incompleteness in 1931.

M56.notes: Goedel, Monatshefte 37 (1930) and 38 (1931) confirmed. Arithmetisation of syntax (Goedel numbering, Chinese remainder theorem) transfers number theory into metamathematics. Conceptual date 1929-30 is in scope.

events.name: Frobenius method and singular ODE theory
events.summary: Fuchs and Frobenius used series in the complex domain to solve linear ODEs with regular singular points.
keyWorks: Fuchs, Zur Theorie der linearen Differentialgleichungen, 1866
Frobenius, Ueber die Integration der linearen Differentialgleichungen durch Reihen, 1873

evidence.paraphrase: Frobenius presented in 1873 a series method for equations with regular singular points.

W78.notes: Fuchs, Crelle 66 (1866) and Frobenius, Crelle 76 (1873) confirmed. Weierstrass-Riemann complex function theory applied to linear ODEs founds the analytic theory of ODEs.

events.name: Wiener process
events.summary: Wiener constructed rigorous measure on Brownian paths.
keyWorks: Wiener, Differential space, J. Math. Phys. 1923

evidence.paraphrase: In 1923 Wiener first treated a continuous Markov process rigorously.

M73.notes: Wiener, J. Math. Phys. 2 (1923) confirmed. Daniell-Lebesgue integration applied to physical Brownian motion (Einstein 1905, Bachelier 1900).

events.name: Several complex variables and Hartogs
events.summary: Hartogs discovered phenomena, such as automatic extension of holomorphic functions, with no one-variable analogue.
keyWorks: Hartogs, Zur Theorie der analytischen Funktionen mehrerer unabhaengiger Veraenderlichen, 1906

evidence.paraphrase: Several complex variables generalises one-variable complex analysis to higher complex dimension.

W82.notes: Hartogs, Math. Ann. 62 (1906) confirmed; the full title continues 'insbesondere ueber die Darstellung derselben durch Reihen...'. Weierstrass and Poincare earlier studied several variables, but the Hartogs phenomena mark the split.

events.name: Abstract rings and fields
events.summary: Dedekind, Weber, Steinitz and Fraenkel gave axiomatic definitions of fields and rings, culminating in van der Waerden's textbook.
keyWorks: Weber, Die allgemeinen Grundlagen der Galois'schen Gleichungstheorie, Math. Ann. 1893
Steinitz, Algebraische Theorie der Koerper, Crelle 1910
van der Waerden, Moderne Algebra, 1930-31

evidence.paraphrase: Steinitz in 1910 gave the modern axiomatic field definition and van der Waerden reoriented algebra toward structures.

W65.notes: Weber, Math. Ann. 43 (1893), Steinitz 1910 and van der Waerden 1930 confirmed. Broad and overlapping M27 and M28. Consider restricting it to rings (Fraenkel 1914) or merging.

events.name: Decision problems for groups (Dehn)
events.summary: Dehn posed word, conjugacy and isomorphism problems for finitely presented groups, motivated by topology.
keyWorks: Dehn, Ueber unendliche diskontinuierliche Gruppen, Math. Ann. 1911

evidence.paraphrase: Dehn belongs to the developers of groups defined by generators and relations.

W70.notes: Dehn, Math. Ann. 71 (1911) confirmed. Topology (3-manifolds, knots) supplies the decision problems, founding combinatorial group theory. Formal logic is not a source in 1911.

events.name: Operator algebras
events.summary: Von Neumann introduced self-adjoint operator algebras.
keyWorks: von Neumann, Zur Algebra der Funktionaloperationen, Math. Ann. 1929-30

evidence.paraphrase: 1929 paper introduced weakly closed operator algebras.

M67.notes: von Neumann, Math. Ann. 102 is dated 1930 (received 1929); confirmed. Motivated by quantum mechanics. Rings of operators: Murray and von Neumann 1936.

events.name: Descriptive set theory
events.summary: Baire, Lebesgue, Suslin and Lusin explored regularity of definable sets, leading to analytic and projective sets.
keyWorks: Suslin, Sur une definition des ensembles measurables B, 1917
Lusin, Lecons sur les ensembles analytiques, 1930

evidence.paraphrase: Suslin found an error in 1917, and Lusin's 1930 book consolidated analytic sets.

M39.notes: Suslin, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 164 (1917) is not in Crossref but well attested; Lusin's Lecons (1930) confirmed. Roots: Baire 1899, Lebesgue 1905.

events.name: Schur: polynomial representations of GL(n) and invariant theory
events.summary: Schur's thesis used Frobenius methods to classify rational representations of the general linear group, tying them to symmetric functions.
keyWorks: Schur, Ueber eine Klasse von Matrizen, die sich einer gegebenen Matrix zuordnen lassen, thesis 1901

evidence.paraphrase: His 1901 thesis treated rational representations of GL over the complex numbers, introducing S-functions.

M21.notes: Schur's 1901 Berlin thesis confirmed via Gesammelte Abhandlungen. A dictionary between polynomial representations of GL(n) and symmetric functions.

events.name: Klein model: consistency of non-Euclidean geometry within projective geometry
events.summary: Klein showed Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometries are special cases of projective geometry with a conic, making them equally consistent.
keyWorks: Klein, Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie, Math. Ann. 1871 and 1873
Cayley, A sixth memoir upon quantics, 1859

evidence.paraphrase: The 1871 papers treat both geometries as projective surfaces with a conic, showing equal consistency.

M18.notes: Klein, Math. Ann. 4 (1871) and 6 (1873) confirmed; Cayley's sixth memoir is Phil. Trans. 149 (1859). Projective metric gives relative consistency. Beltrami 1868 is a parallel model.

events.name: Peano's vector space axioms
events.summary: Peano gave a modern axiomatic definition of vector space after Grassmann.
keyWorks: Peano, Calcolo geometrico, 1888

evidence.paraphrase: The 1888 book gave the first definition of a vector space in a modern style.

M51.notes: Peano's Calcolo geometrico (1888) confirmed. An axiomatic abstraction from Grassmann; little uptake until Weyl 1918 and Banach 1922. Logic is not a real source field.

events.name: Riemann-Hilbert problem and monodromy
events.summary: Riemann asked for a differential equation with prescribed monodromy group, and Plemelj attacked it with singular integral equations.
keyWorks: Plemelj, Riemannsche Funktionenscharen mit gegebener Monodromiegruppe, Monatsh. Math. 1908

evidence.paraphrase: Plemelj in 1908 solved the Riemann problem of a differential equation with a given monodromy group.

W77.notes: Monodromy problem (Riemann 1857; Hilbert's 21st problem 1900) attacked with singular integral equations. Monatsh. Math. Phys. 19 (1908), doi 10.1007/bf01736697. Note that Plemelj's solution has a gap (Bolibruch 1989 counterexample).

events.name: Weyl's Riemann surface and abstract manifold concept
events.summary: Weyl gave a rigorous definition of Riemann surface as a topological manifold with charts.
keyWorks: Weyl, Die Idee der Riemannschen Flaeche, 1913

evidence.paraphrase: The 1913 work unified analysis, geometry, and topology.

M63.notes: Weyl's book (Teubner 1913, in Open Library) gave the first intrinsic definition of a manifold by charts and neighbourhoods. It fuses topology and function theory. Better seen as the birth of the abstract manifold concept than as reification.

events.name: Noncommutative algebras, representation theory and number theory
from: algebraic number theory (class field theory, p-adic local theory)
events.summary: Noether, Brauer and Hasse linked hypercomplex systems to commutative algebra and arithmetic via modules and cohomological ideas.
keyWorks: Brauer, Hasse, Noether, Beweis eines Hauptsatzes in der Theorie der Algebren, Crelle 1932

evidence.paraphrase: Work on noncommutative algebras began in 1927 and the main theorem appeared in 1932.

M29.notes: Arithmetic local-global methods settle the classification of central simple algebras over number fields: they are all cyclic. Crelle 167 (1932), doi 10.1515/crll.1932.167.399. The conceptual date is within scope (Brauer group 1928, Hasse's local theory 1931).

events.name: Dirichlet principle: potential theory as a tool for function theory
events.summary: Riemann used a variational minimum principle from potential theory to guarantee existence of functions on surfaces; Weierstrass's criticism led to Hilbert's repaired form.
keyWorks: Riemann, thesis 1851
Hilbert, Ueber das Dirichletsche Princip, 1901

evidence.paraphrase: Riemann's use of the variational principle was shown flawed by Weierstrass and rescued by Hilbert in 1901.

M5.notes: Genuine import. Hilbert's rescue was published in Jahresber. DMV 8 (1900) 184-188, then Math. Ann. 59 (1904); the date is 1900, not 1901. Riemann's thesis (1851) and the Crelle 54 paper (1857) are the methodological uses.

events.name: Mathematical biology
events.summary: Volterra and Lotka modeled predator-prey dynamics.
keyWorks: Volterra, Variazioni e fluttuazioni, 1926

evidence.paraphrase: He turned to mathematical biology after WWI.

M79.notes: The name 'mathematical biology' is too broad: Verhulst (1838) and Ross (1911) came earlier. The event is Lotka-Volterra predator-prey dynamics. Volterra's Memorie Lincei paper is cited as 1926 (the English version is in Nature 118, 1926, doi 10.1038/118558a0). Lotka's Elements of Physical Biology (1925) is in Open Library.

events.name: Subjective probability and decision
events.summary: Keynes, Ramsey and de Finetti defined probability as degree of belief, reviving Bayesian ideas against frequentism.
keyWorks: Keynes, A Treatise on Probability, 1921
Ramsey, Truth and Probability, 1926
de Finetti, Funzione caratteristica di un fenomeno aleatorio, 1930

evidence.paraphrase: Keynes proposed probability as belief in the early 1920s and de Finetti and Ramsey developed it.

W61.notes: Borderline. Ramsey's Truth and Probability was written in 1926 but published only in 1931, in The Foundations of Mathematics (in Open Library). De Finetti's key subjective paper is Fund. Math. 17 (1931), doi 10.4064/fm-17-1-298-329. Keynes 1921 is logical, not subjective, probability. The decision-theory fusion is the genuine part.

events.name: Hasse local-global principle
events.summary: Hasse showed a quadratic form represents zero over the rationals when it does so over all completions.
keyWorks: Hasse, Ueber die Darstellbarkeit von Zahlen durch quadratische Formen im Koerper der rationalen Zahlen, Crelle 1923

evidence.paraphrase: Hasse discovered the principle in October 1920 under Hensel and used it in his 1921 thesis.

M12.notes: Crelle 152 (1923), doi 10.1515/crll.1923.152.129; this is the thesis of 1921. Borderline as a single-field event, but the bridge from local (analytic) completions to global arithmetic is the genuine part.

events.name: Consistency models of non-Euclidean geometry
events.summary: Beltrami and Klein built models of hyperbolic geometry inside Euclidean or projective geometry, showing the parallel postulate independent of the other axioms.
keyWorks: Beltrami, Saggio di interpretazione della geometria non-euclidea, 1868
Klein, Ueber die sogenannte Nicht-Euklidische Geometrie, Math. Ann. 1871

evidence.paraphrase: Beltrami showed in 1868 that the parallel postulate is independent of the other axioms, and Klein modelled it analytically in 1870.

W2.notes: The conceptual date for the models is 1868, not 1829-32 (that is non-Euclidean geometry itself). Klein, Math. Ann. 4 (1871), doi 10.1007/bf02100583. Beltrami 1868 is in the Giornale di Matematiche (no DOI). Not an import from outside.

events.name: Combinatorial group theory and presentations
events.summary: Von Dyck and then Dehn, Nielsen and Schreier studied groups by generators and relations, motivated by fundamental groups of surfaces and knots.
keyWorks: Dehn, Ueber unendliche diskontinuierliche Gruppen, Math. Ann. 1911
Schreier, Die Untergruppen der freien Gruppen, 1927

evidence.paraphrase: Dyck, Dehn, Nielsen and Schreier developed groups defined by generators and relations from 1880 to 1920.

W69.notes: Dyck, Math. Ann. 20 (1882), doi 10.1007/bf01443322. Dehn, Math. Ann. 71 (1911), doi 10.1007/bf01456932. Schreier, Abh. Hamburg 5 (1927), doi 10.1007/bf02952517. Magnus's book (1931) or later is the institutional date.

events.name: Burnside's use of character theory for finite group theory
events.summary: Burnside applied Frobenius characters to prove the p^a q^b solvability theorem.
keyWorks: Burnside, Theory of Groups of Finite Order, 1897 and 2nd ed. 1911
Burnside, On groups of order p^a q^b, 1904

evidence.paraphrase: His 1904 solvability result for groups of order p^m q^n applied character methods.

M22.notes: Proc. LMS s2-1 (1904), doi 10.1112/plms/s2-1.1.388. A clean technique transfer, with representation theory settling a structural question.
